In this situation it is not accurate to pass errno.  We don't know why the pointer is nullptr.  It could be a firmware error, or it could be an I2C error.  Since we don't have an I2CException, we don't have a valid captured errno value.

errno is set by many C functions, and it is difficult to know when those functions are called by higher level C++ code.  So unless you capture the value right where the failure occurs, there is a good chance another line of C/C++ code calls a function that modifies errno.

I'd suggest modifying the last parameter of reportI2CPel() to default to "0".  That is a safe value indicating no problem within errno.  You could also just change the parameter to be an int and default to 0.

Then in cases like this where you want to call reportI2CPel() but you don't have a valid errno value, you can just omit that parameter.

This comment applies to all places where you call reportI2CPel() but did not catch an I2CException with the captured errno value.

As discussed above, the value of errno could have been modified by other code since the failure occurred.

You can just change your catch to
```
catch (const i2c::I2CException& e)
```

and then get the captured errno value from `e.errorCode`.  The exception contains the captured errno value.

This same comment applies to all other places where you catch an exception from the I2CInterface class.
